title: Reopened bisector on IMG_4111's tail: a stray saved end anchor makes the cut loop back, its end cannot be deleted, editing is laggy, and Esc does not leave the bisector
description:
Reported by the user 2026-10-24 on master (after CRAW-73, CRAW-75, TOOL-41), in the ring scene on crawfish IMG_4111, tail, right side; screenshots in the session.
1. A bisector running along the right side of tail segments 3 to 6 has a yellow end anchor on the tail_segment_4/5 dorsal boundary that the user never placed. The bisector doubles back from it (two red lines with a black sliver band between them along segments 3-5). Suspect: the initial start/end (the waiting first end, or the ends snapped at creation) were saved as an end and an inner anchor, so the cut goes out and back. It is in the saved DSL on master, so find which statement/anchors produce it and how the save wrote them.
2. Selecting that end anchor and pressing X is refused: 'inner anchors hold the bisector between its ends; delete them first, or drag the end along a wall'. The user has other bisector anchors at wall edges (e.g. by region 54, the first point's neighbour) and expects to delete the end there: deleting an end should promote the nearest remaining anchor on a wall to be the new end, or the refusal must say exactly what to do.
3. Moving and placing points on this bisector is very laggy. Profile it (async-profiler via run-scene --profile) on the crawfish and fix the hot path.
4. Esc does not leave the bisector. The user pressed Ctrl+R (ring tool), then clicked this existing bisector, which reopens it as a bisector draft in the bisector sub-tool (CRAW-73). CRAW-73 changed Esc on an edited bisector draft to keep the draft and go to orbit; check what actually happens and whether the reopened draft is owned by the bisector sub-tool at all. The user expects Esc to leave the bisector.
definition-of-done:
1. Root cause of the stray end and the loop-back found and fixed at the source; the IMG_4111 bisector corrected only through the tool and its save (no hand edits), with a regression test that the save writes exactly the anchors the user placed.
2. An end anchor can be deleted when another anchor can take its place on a wall, or the refusal names the anchor to delete.
3. Moving and placing anchors on a crawfish bisector is responsive (before/after timings).
4. Esc leaves the bisector the way the user expects, for a new and a reopened bisector; tests.
testing-plan:
1. mvn test.
2. Live through ixdar-cli on a tmp copy of IMG_4111: reopen the tail bisector, delete the stray end, move an anchor (timed), Esc.
changes-made:
Root cause of the stray end and loop-back: RingTool.confirmDraft, confirming a re-opened bisector, wrote back its anchors but not BisectorTool.draftEnds, so an end dragged onto another wall kept its old wall in confirmedBisectorEnds; the save wrote ends="ring_05; ring_03" while the last point sat on ring_50, and every reload re-attached that end to the nearest ring_03 vertex (the yellow end on the tail_segment_4/5 dorsal boundary), the cut running out to anchor 14 and back. Reproduced from scratch on a tmp IMG_4111 copy (new bisector ring_03->ring_00 saved exactly; re-opened, end dragged to ring_01, saved ends still ring_03; ring_00). Fixed: confirmDraft stores the draft's end walls (and counts a wall change as an edit). Test BisectorTest.aReopenedBisectorWhoseEndMovesToAnotherWallSavesAndReloadsThatWall (fails without the fix).
X on an end (BisectorTool.deletePoint): the anchor next to the end becomes the end when it lies on a wall (within the selected-anchor disc, snapped onto the wall vertex, the end wall switched); else the refusal names the anchors in the way and the nearest anchor on a wall that would take the end's place, or says none lies on a wall. RingTool.snapToWall takes the reach in pixels. Test deletingAnEndPromotesTheAnchorNextToItOntoItsWall.
Lag: async-profiler showed RegionLayer rebuilding the regions (RingRegions.update over all 987k faces, flatness, colours, explosion) on every ring revision, although a re-opened bisector's draft changes no live mask; RegionLayer now skips a revision whose live labels and masks are unchanged (test RegionHidingTest.aRingRevisionThatLeavesEveryMaskAsItWasKeepsTheRegions). BisectorTool.addAnchor traced the whole bisector once per span; it now traces the CANDIDATE_SPANS (3) spans the anchor detours least from by chord length, more only when none takes it. Crawfish ring_68: addAnchor 88-211 ms -> 10-20 ms, placement 281 -> 157 ms, drag step 81 -> 64 ms (idle headless frame ~60 ms); tmp/craw-79-measurements.json.
Esc: Ctrl+R then a click on the bisector does re-open it owned by BisectorTool with the sub-tool switched; an edited draft then went to orbit and Ctrl+R came back to it. Now Esc (and K) always leave the bisector for the rings: an unedited new or re-opened draft closes unrecorded (a new one's waiting end goes too); an edited one is confirmed when Enter would take it, else dropped as an undoable edit (Ctrl+Z restores it in the bisector). Ring drafts keep the CRAW-73 behaviour. Also ClosedRingTool.activate refreshes the controls, which after leaving the bisector still listed its rows (the next K left again instead of bisecting). Tests escLeavesTheBisectorForNewAndReopenedDrafts and the extended aBisectorCannotCrossItself.
IMG_4111.dsl corrected through the ring scene: re-opened ring_68, dragged the stray end from ring_03 back to the user's saved end point, where it snapped onto ring_50 exactly at the user's vertex, Enter, Ctrl+S. Only ring_68's ends changed (ring_05; ring_03 -> ring_05; ring_50); all 16 points identical. Screenshots tmp/craw-79-img4111-before*.png and tmp/craw-79-img4111-after*.png. mvn test 672 run, 0 failed.

Follow-up (user rulings: no sub-tool type checks; each sub-tool's info lives in its own class). RingTool, RegionLayer and the sub-tools no longer compare sub-tool instances: new RingSubTool methods, overridden by ClosedRingTool and BisectorTool, are reopens(ConfirmedRing) (which sub-tool re-opens a confirmed ring), wallsWhileDrafted() (a new draft previewed as a wall in the region colours), showsRegions() (region colours while active; RegionLayer asks RingTool.activeRingSubTool()), nothingToConfirm() (Enter's refusal with no draft), escapeEditedDraft() (Esc on an edited draft: ring keeps it and leaves the key to the scene, bisector confirms or drops it and leaves), escapeAfterUneditedDraft() (what Esc does after an unedited draft closed: the bisector drops its waiting end and leaves), and escapeDescription() now whole per sub-tool (RingTool returns the active one's). Moved out of RingTool: BISECTOR_REACH_PIXELS (now BisectorTool.END_REACH_PIXELS), snapToWall with snappedWall and the wall/snap scratch arrays (BisectorTool), DRAFT_LABEL, REMOVE_SELECTED_ANCHOR_HINT and RING_HIT_PIXELS (ClosedRingTool). Behaviour unchanged: BisectorTest/CreaseRingTest/RingEscapeTest/RegionHidingTest pass, mvn test 676 run 0 failed, and redoing the ring_68 correction on a fresh copy of master's IMG_4111 saves the same statement (ends ring_05; ring_50, the 16 points) with the same fingerprint 3ed39f987347011f.
review-summary: RingTool now keeps a re-opened bisector's new end wall when it is confirmed, BisectorTool lets an end go to a neighbour on a wall and leaves on Esc, and RegionLayer skips rebuilds that change no ring. A saved bisector reloaded onto its old wall and doubled back.
